finding.summary: Session serialization accumulates the complete, potentially large session payload in a default growable MemoryStream.
finding.explanation: CommitAsync serializes every key and value into a default MemoryStream with repeated writes and no validated capacity bound, then calls ToArray for an additional full copy. Large or bursty session state can therefore cause geometric backing-array growth, LOH pressure, and high peak memory on the request path.

finding.summary: Authentication properties serialize through an unbounded growable MemoryStream.
finding.explanation: Serialize writes all authentication property entries into a default MemoryStream without a validated capacity or serialized-size bound and then calls ToArray. Large property collections or values can cause repeated growth copies and a second exact-size allocation.

finding.summary: Render-tree keyed lookup probes each old sibling key before inserting it.
finding.explanation: BuildKeyToInfoLookup calls ContainsKey(key) to detect a duplicate and then assigns result[key] for the same key. The pooled plain Dictionary therefore hashes and probes every nonduplicate old key twice on a render-diff path. A single TryAdd-style operation can preserve duplicate detection and exception behavior while avoiding the second probe.

finding.summary: Password validation uses LINQ All to scan every UTF-16 character.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync routes the non-alphanumeric requirement through Enumerable.All over the password string. This is a reusable validation path and the predicate is a simple character test; a direct indexed loop preserves short-circuiting and works across every target framework without LINQ iterator and delegate overhead.

finding.summary: Password digit validation uses LINQ Any over the string.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync enumerates password characters through Enumerable.Any for a simple digit predicate. A direct indexed loop is portable to the project’s .NET Framework, netstandard2.0, and modern .NET targets and preserves the existing UTF-16 char semantics and short-circuiting.

finding.summary: Password lowercase validation uses LINQ Any over the string.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync enumerates password characters through Enumerable.Any for a simple lowercase predicate. A direct indexed loop avoids LINQ enumeration while preserving short-circuiting and exact char-category behavior on all target frameworks.

finding.summary: Password uppercase validation uses LINQ Any over the string.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync enumerates password characters through Enumerable.Any for a simple uppercase predicate. A direct indexed loop avoids LINQ enumeration while preserving short-circuiting and exact char-category behavior on all target frameworks.

finding.summary: Username validation enumerates the username with LINQ and searches the allowed-character string for every character.
finding.explanation: ValidateUserName runs for each Identity user validation operation. Its Any predicate enumerates the string through LINQ, and each predicate invocation performs another sequential character search over the configurable AllowedUserNameCharacters string. A direct indexed loop can preserve the current UTF-16 char semantics, null/empty handling, and short-circuit behavior without LINQ iterator/delegate overhead.

finding.summary: Stream IDs are accumulated in a temporary List and immediately copied to an array.
finding.explanation: ReadStreamIds knows streamIdCount before parsing, but allocates a growable List<string>, appends every ID, then allocates and copies again with ToArray. The list is only an intermediate adapter for the string[] return value on the per-message MessagePack parse path. Allocate the final array from streamIdCount and fill it directly while preserving null-for-empty behavior and validation order.

finding.summary: Authentication ticket serialization grows a MemoryStream and then copies the complete ticket.
finding.explanation: Serialize writes a ticket with variable identity, claim, property, and string counts through BinaryWriter into a default MemoryStream, then returns ToArray. The source does not enforce a local serialized-size bound, so unusually large tickets can cause repeated growth and a final full copy. The public byte[] contract and wire compatibility make the final owned array necessary; any optimization must preserve format version, field ordering, encoding, and exception behavior.

finding.summary: Compression negotiation fully sorts candidates to select one provider.
finding.explanation: On the multi-candidate request path, the code orders every ProviderCandidate by quality and priority and immediately takes First(). A single-pass best-candidate selection would avoid the full sort. The expected candidate set is normally small, so the occurrence is retained at low severity despite being on a per-request path.

finding.summary: WebTransport session disposal blocks on each stream’s asynchronous disposal while holding the stream lock.
finding.explanation: The synchronous session Dispose path calls DisposeAsync().AsTask().GetAwaiter().GetResult() for every open stream while holding _openStreams. WebTransportStream disposal awaits registration and pipe completion, so this can block a shared server thread and prolong lock ownership for every stream in the session.

finding.summary: Validation-summary fallback rescans a growing list for every model-state entry.
finding.explanation: GetModelStateList builds a List<ModelStateEntry> using Visit. When entries.Count is less than ModelState.Count, it iterates the entire model-state dictionary and performs entries.Contains(entry.Value) on each iteration. Each membership operation scans the retained list, which grows as unmatched entries are appended. This has quadratic worst-case comparison cost in that fallback branch. DefaultHtmlGenerator.GenerateValidationSummary calls the helper at line 844. Build a HashSet<ModelStateEntry> only when the fallback is required and retain the list for rendering order, using the same default equality semantics. Branch reachability and timing have not been exercised at runtime.
finding.recommended_fix: Only when entering the unmatched-entry fallback, build a HashSet<ModelStateEntry> alongside the ordered rendering list.
finding.compatibility_notes: Preserve default equality semantics, rendering order, and the existing list contract. The model-binding producer and runtime impact remain unverified.

finding.summary: JSON Patch value conversion allocates a JSON string solely to deserialize it into the property type.
finding.explanation: ConvertTo short-circuits null and assignable values, but both non-assignable branches call SerializeObject(value) directly inside DeserializeObject. That JSON text has no other consumer. JsonPatchDocument.ApplyTo loops through operations; Operation.Apply dispatches Add, ObjectAdapter.Add resolves the target adapter, and PocoAdapter.TryAdd calls TryConvertValue, which calls this helper. Thus conversion can allocate and process a throwaway JSON string for each applicable patch operation. The serializer conversion itself is intentional; this finding concerns its text bridge, not a proposal to remove conversion or preserve mutable aliases. No throughput or allocation trace was run, and gains from a token-based bridge remain unmeasured.
finding.recommended_fix: Within the existing internal conversion seam, evaluate a Json.NET JTokenWriter/JTokenReader bridge (or direct ToObject for compatible already-materialized tokens) instead of allocating JSON text. Retain the assignability fast path and public signatures. Use separate serialization and deserialization configurations matching the current defaults and supplied resolver, and preserve the fallback where direct conversion changes semantics. Do not replace CopyTo with returning the original mutable value.
finding.compatibility_notes: Json.NET token readers/writers are package APIs available across this project's net462, netstandard2.0 and net12.0 targets; no modern-only BCL API or public API redesign is required. Preserve JsonConvert.DefaultSettings participation, converters, resolver asymmetry (currently only the deserialization settings receive the supplied resolver), date/float/numeric/string conversion, independent-copy semantics, and caught failures returning CanBeConverted=false. The direct path must be validated for these contracts before adoption; source inspection proves the throwaway text shape, not equivalence or performance of a replacement.

finding.summary: JSON Patch list operations repeatedly rediscover the closed IList<T> interface.
finding.explanation: TryAdd, TryGet, TryRemove, TryReplace, TryTest and TryTraverse all call TryGetListTypeArgument. For ordinary List<T> receivers, ClosedGenericMatcher cannot take its query-type-is-IList<T> shortcut and calls Type.GetInterfaces in GetGenericInstantiation, scanning the returned array and potentially recursing through base types. Neither ListAdapter nor the fully read helper caches this discovery. ObjectVisitor invokes adapter traversal for each interior path segment, and the default AdapterFactory constructs a new ListAdapter for IList targets, so adapter instances do not amortize the lookup. This establishes repeated reflection on the per-operation/per-segment path, not measured latency or CPU impact.
finding.recommended_fix: Cache the resolved closed IList<T> interface or its element Type by runtime list Type in an internal, appropriately scoped metadata cache, then reuse it for list validation and operations. Preserve unsupported-array/non-generic-list checks and failure messages; avoid changing the public API.
finding.compatibility_notes: Type-keyed metadata caching is available on all relevant .NET targets and requires no newer API. Preserve the helper's deterministic selection when multiple IList<T> implementations exist, recursive base-type behavior, null/error semantics, trimming annotations, concurrent access, and metadata-update/type-lifetime behavior. Do not turn arbitrary dynamically produced runtime types into a permanently growing cache without lifecycle bounds. Owning csproj uses DefaultNetCoreTargetFramework, resolved to net12.0 in eng/Versions.props.

finding.summary: Stored component/TempData serialization grows a contiguous MemoryStream and then copies the full payload.
finding.explanation: SerializeData and SerializeValue construct default growable MemoryStreams, write JSON through Utf8JsonWriter and return ToArray. Allowed values include strings and collections, with no size bound in this serializer. SessionStorageTempDataProvider.SaveTempData serializes nonempty data before session.Set, establishing a persistence request consumer. Large encoded data can therefore cause backing-array growth copies plus an exact result copy; actual payload frequency and allocation magnitude remain unmeasured.
finding.recommended_fix: Consider an internal pooled/segmented UTF-8 buffer writer and make only the final independent byte[] copy required by IStoredDataSerializer. If a valid exact encoded length is available, pre-size instead. Do not remove the owned byte[] boundary or impose new limits without the storage contract permitting it.
finding.compatibility_notes: Keep JSON type tokens, options, ordering, complete output before storage, exception timing and independent array ownership. Utf8JsonWriter accepts IBufferWriter<byte> on the existing modern target; pooled scratch storage needs deterministic return and bounded retention. No public API change is recommended.

finding.summary: Duplicate tool-name detection probes the same dictionary key before insertion.

finding.summary: Tool parameter parsing performs a dictionary membership probe before insertion.
finding.explanation: The source generator calls ContainsKey for each discovered tool parameter and then assigns the same key through the indexer. A successful new entry therefore performs separate lookup and insertion probes. TryAdd can preserve duplicate detection while avoiding the second probe; this is source-generation work, so it is informational.

finding.summary: Tool result parsing performs a dictionary membership probe before insertion.
finding.explanation: The source generator calls ContainsKey for each discovered result key and then assigns that same key through the indexer. TryAdd can preserve the duplicate diagnostic and avoid a second dictionary probe. This runs during source generation and is therefore informational.

finding.summary: Metadata collision handling probes the same dictionary key again on update.
finding.explanation: The method owns a plain Dictionary<string,object> with StringComparer.Ordinal. After TryGetValue(property.Name), the duplicate non-inherited-property branch assigns a new collision list through dictionary[property.Name], repeating a key lookup. ComponentProperties obtains this metadata during WritersForType construction and caches writers by Type, so this is metadata setup/refresh work, not a per-render allocation finding. The ref-based modern optimization would be optional and its value here is unmeasured.
finding.recommended_fix: If profiling justifies optimizing metadata construction, use a private single-probe slot update on supported modern targets, releasing any dictionary ref before further dictionary mutation or yield. Preserve the current inherited-property filtering, Ordinal comparer and collision-list behavior; otherwise leave this cold path alone.
finding.compatibility_notes: CollectionsMarshal ref APIs require modern .NET and careful iterator/ref lifetimes. No public signature change is needed. Preserve dictionary duplicate behavior, reflection ordering and hot-reload writer-cache invalidation.

finding.summary: Asset-label indexing probes the same dictionary key before insertion.

finding.summary: Import-map scope merging probes the same dictionary key twice.

finding.summary: Key-ring construction checks for the default key before adding it.

finding.summary: The nested test controller returns a fresh stateless EmptyResult.

finding.summary: Recursive directory results are materialized before one concatenation

finding.summary: A Take projection is copied to an array before one string.Join use.

The code does not index, reuse, or mutate the materialized list, and the source symbol collections remain stable for the enumeration, so the List and its backing array are avoidable. finding.summary: xUnit failure-message formatting eagerly joins browser logs
finding.explanation: The interpolated Assert.True message calls string.Join before Assert.True evaluates the predicate, so the complete browser-log sequence is joined even when the assertion succeeds. This is test-only and therefore informational.

finding.summary: Windows identity lookup is evaluated before the log level can filter the event
finding.explanation: WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent().Name is computed as a logging argument before the logger extension can decide whether to emit the event. Encryption/key-persistence frequency is low, so the occurrence is retained as informational.

finding.summary: Node stderr lines are regex-normalized before the logger filters Error.
finding.explanation: The stderr line callback calls LogError(StripAnsiColors(line)); StripAnsiColors invokes AnsiColorRegex.Replace. Argument evaluation occurs even when Error logging is disabled. The neighboring stdout path explicitly checks Information before performing the same normalization. This is shipped development-server process-output handling, not a production request-hot path; disabled-Error configuration and performance impact were not exercised.
finding.recommended_fix: Guard the Error-level branch with logger.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Error), matching the existing stdout pattern, before calling StripAnsiColors.
finding.compatibility_notes: Use the existing logging API, preserve Error level and exact ANSI stripping. Delaying the regex call changes when its exceptions occur; do not apply if that normalization has required side effects outside logging. No public API or new dependency is required.

finding.summary: The byte-comparison loop eagerly formats an assertion message for every successful element check.
finding.explanation: Assert.True is an ordinary call, so its interpolated message is constructed before the assertion examines the condition. The loop performs 8,193 element checks and eagerly evaluates three interpolation holes, including two array indexers, even when every byte matches. This is test-only work, so it is informational, while still matching the card's assertion-message hard-keep rule.

finding.summary: A Trace.Assert failure message eagerly formats an enum on successful checks.
finding.explanation: When TRACE is included, headersFrame.Type.ToString() is evaluated before Trace.Assert inspects the condition, even though the message is only useful when the assertion fails. This occurs in a single-exchange diagnostic sample, so it is informational.

finding.summary: A data frame is copied and UTF-8 decoded before Information logging is gated.
finding.explanation: The LogInformation argument calls ReadOnlySequence.ToArray and Encoding.UTF8.GetString before the logger can test whether Information is enabled. The sample performs this for its received DATA frame; because the site is a small diagnostic sample rather than a production server path, it is informational.

finding.summary: Each browser message schedules a separate thread-pool task.
finding.explanation: The WebMessageReceived callback invokes Task.Factory.StartNew for every incoming message and the scheduled delegate only computes the fixed origin and forwards the message. Message volume therefore directly creates fine-grained task scheduling overhead. The occurrence is in sample platform code, so it is classified informational.

finding.summary: A fixed four-element encoding table is retained as List<Encoding>.
finding.explanation: SupportedEncodings is private, static, fixed after initialization, and is indexed by Count and indexer in media-type detection. An Encoding[] would represent the fixed positional data with less collection machinery. The list is tiny and process-wide, so the expected impact is informational.

finding.summary: Generic dictionary null guards permit a value-type instantiation, but allocation remains unproven.
finding.explanation: TKey is constrained only to notnull, so key==null in TryAdd has the generic object-conversion shape covered by the card. Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.csproj links this source. The inspected QueryFeature and RequestCookieCollection instantiate string keys, not structs; modern JITs can remove non-nullable value-type boxing. The finding deliberately does not claim actual heap allocation or a reachable struct-key hotspot in the inspected shipping callers.
finding.recommended_fix: Do not change the current string-key paths solely from this pattern. First identify a shipping struct-key workload and inspect target-runtime generated code/allocation data; only if boxing survives, gate the private generic guard by a cached type trait while retaining reference/nullable null rejection.
finding.compatibility_notes: notnull is a nullable-analysis constraint, not class-only. Adding class would narrow the generic contract and is not recommended. An internal trait must handle Nullable<T> deliberately; is null or ThrowIfNull alone is not a cross-runtime guarantee against boxing.

finding.summary: The source-generator model combines field hashes with multiplication and XOR.
finding.explanation: GetHashCode combines two string hash codes using a hand-written multiply-and-XOR formula. HashCode.Combine provides a maintained combiner on newer targets, but this generator targets netstandard2.0, so adopting it requires compatibility consideration. The type is used by build-time generator infrastructure, making the finding informational.

finding.summary: NameValueHeaderValue combines its order-significant identity fields using XOR only.
finding.explanation: GetHashCode XORs the name hash with the value hash, making the combination commutative and permitting equal component hashes to cancel. No in-repository hash-container use of NameValueHeaderValue was established, so the card requires an informational classification.

finding.summary: Named-pipe endpoint identity fields are combined with XOR only.

finding.summary: Each LoadItems call rediscovers compiled-item attributes through reflection.
finding.explanation: LoadAttributes calls Assembly.GetCustomAttributes<RazorCompiledItemAttribute>() on every LoadItems invocation, with no metadata cache. The normal use is startup-oriented, so this is informational rather than a hot-path defect. Any cache must preserve per-call list ownership and the virtual CreateItem customization boundary.

finding.summary: The emitted runtime parameter resolver repeats attribute reflection for each resolution.
finding.explanation: TryGetValidatableParameterInfo performs multiple GetCustomAttribute/GetCustomAttributes lookups and materializes validation attributes each time, with no cache in the resolver or ValidationOptions. Parameter metadata resolution is normally endpoint construction/startup work rather than per-request validation, so the uncached reflection is retained as informational.

finding.summary: Generated type metadata re-runs GetInterfaces when resolver results are reconstructed.
finding.explanation: The snapshot shows each GeneratedValidatableTypeInfo constructor calling Type.GetInterfaces. The generated resolver creates new type-info instances for successful lookups, so recursive/per-value validation can repeat this reflection. The assigned file is a generator golden snapshot rather than compiled product code, so the emitted hot-path shape is informational.

finding.summary: Generated property validation rediscovers PropertyInfo on every value access.
finding.explanation: The generated Property accessor calls DeclaringType.GetProperty each time validation reads a property and then uses reflective GetValue. Property validation runs per member and recursively for collection elements, and this PropertyInfo is not cached. The file is a generator golden snapshot, so the occurrence is informational.
finding.snippet: private PropertyInfo Property => DeclaringType.GetProperty(Name, BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly);

finding.summary: An enum is converted to a string and then uppercased before constructing an exception.
finding.explanation: The throw helper calls HttpMethod.ToString() and then ToUpperInvariant(), producing the enum-name string and a second normalized string. This is the card's fixed-value ToString-plus-casing shape. It is retained as informational because it runs only on a bad-request exception path.
